text.p: Metals recycler Simsmetal Ltd said on Tuesday it anticipated improved profitability in the current year to June 30, 1998, provided there was no deterioration in world metal markets and after contributions from recent acquisitions.
Simsmetal also released its unaudited 1996/97 profits showing a 25 percent fall in net profit to A$35.17 million.
Group profit before interest and tax fell 21 percent to A$$57.64 million on a 19 percent rise in total sales to 4.7 million tonnes.
Fourth quarter net profit rose 64 percent to A$13.109 million and second half earnings were 50 percent higher.
Operating revenues for the year fell marginally to A$1.15 billion, Simsmetal said.
"Simsmetal enters fiscal 1998 seeking growth through acquisitions in all the regions in which it operates world-wide," Simsmetal managing director John Crabb said in a statement.
"Provided there is no deterioration in global metal markets, and including the contribution from recent acquisitions, the Group anticipates improved profitability," he said.
Crabb said earnings and profit margins in the first half were affected by lower global economic growth rates, a stronger Australian dollar and lower secondary metals prices.

"Ferrous and non-ferrous metal prices increased towards the end of the first half resulting in a robust second half and a particularly strong fourth quarter with most operations performing at above forecast levels," Crabb said.
He said while some regions saw lower volumes which affected unit costs, operating costs in the United States and New Zealand improved.

Crabb said the Pick 'n Payless Self Serve Auto Parts business, launched at Blacktown in Sydney in February 1997, was now achieving forecast returns and would contribute positively to the Group's results in 1997/98.

The performance of Simsmetal's U.S. ferrous division improved throughout the year and the Mill Services division achieved record volumes and profitability. U.S. non-ferrous trading also made a strong recovery in the second half, he said.
Simsmetal's British operations recovered in the second half and had record profitability levels in the fourth quarter.
Crabb said a final dividend announcement was expected towards the end of August.
Simsmetal's shares were up five cents at A$10.35 by 10.40 a.m. (0040 GMT).
